Four committed snapshots moved (tab-as-numbers, timesig-grandstaff, tempo-swing, drum-groove) -- systems whose silhouette-binding ink was a beamed member's fixed 3.5 stem now space by the drawn beam; see the re-base commit.

system.beam-over-notes.why: The mirror of system.beam-under-notes: BSD binds the lower system's top ink against a beam coming down, BSU the upper system's bottom ink against one going up -- two edges of one gap through two different skylines. d''' (LilyPond d'''', D7) sits +16 above the middle line, the exact reflection of g,,'s -16 below it, and quant, shorten and thickness are direction-symmetric, so LilyPond prints the same 13.790000 (measured identical) and the two must agree at every stage; a difference between them is a defect on its own, the property P/Q, TU/TD, SD/SU, BMD/BMU and TSD/TSU are all built on. The full account -- the TSD pitch design, the forced-stem shorten, the LP constant decomposition and the seed plan -- is on system.beam-under-notes. PREDICTION: reads the IDENTICAL residual as BSD at every stage (+0.760000 at opening, 0 exact after the seed). MEASURED at opening: reads exactly 14.550000 for a residual of +0.760000, IDENTICAL to BSD -- the pair held to the digit. SEEDED AND CLOSED to 0 exact, IDENTICAL to BSD at every stage (+0.760000 at opening, 0 after the seed) -- the pair held to the digit. The seed's actual location (the BASE BuildSystemSkylines, not AugmentSkylinesForPaging as planned -- a merge is a max, so the stale stem had to be suppressed at its source) is recorded on system.beam-under-notes.

system.clef-bounded-distance.why: Was +0.127272488, closed to -0.000826686 by seeding the clef and by giving this path LilyPond's padding. What is left is one sliver, shared with the stretched pair, and it is now MEASURED rather than inferred: probes/glyph-skyline.ly asks the Clef grob for both of its numbers at once and gets ext = (-2.550 . 4.800) but vertical-skylines = (-2.540 . 4.776). With Y-offset -1.0 that puts the clef's SKYLINE 3.540 below the staff refpoint where its own stencil reaches 3.550 -- exactly the 3.540 this chain works back to. Lily# seeds the LILC bbox, so it is 0.010 too deep. The same probe shows a notehead's skyline and stencil agreeing to the digit (both 0.545), which is why 22120764 closed exactly; the difference is specific to glyphs whose outline curves away from the bbox corner, because LilyPond builds a glyph skyline from the stencil's drawing primitives (stencil-integral.cc) and not from its extent. Closing it needs an outline-based skyline builder, which Lily# has no OTF parser for -- so this stays as a named residual rather than a fitted constant. Original entry follows. The system spring of the same chain as page.clef.first-staff-refpoint, on the same full page 1 of book S, uniform across all 12 gaps in LilyPond's dump. PREDICTION: 12.382500, residual +0.127500, from the same solve -- Lily#'s last-bottom floor is 1.000000 short of LilyPond's because the clef is missing from its skyline, and that slack is spread over the chain. This is the larger of the pair and the one to watch: it is ten times page.clef.first-staff-refpoint's, because the system springs carry inverse stretch 60 against the top spring's 6. ★★ MOVED BY THE GLYPH-SKYLINE PORT 2026-07-28: a grob whose vertical-skylines come from its STENCIL is spaced by the glyph's OUTLINE, not by the designed LILC box its extent is (scm/define-grobs.scm:902 Clef and :35 Accidental, against lily/grob.cc:85-89 simple_vertical_skylines_from_extents which NoteHead:2595 falls back to). The two boxes differ by 0.024 above and 0.010 below on the G clef, 0.448 below on the F clef. Closed from -0.000826686 to -2.40e-7. The 'LILC-vs-skyline sliver' was never a scale: a Clef's skyline is its outline.

line-start.clef-to-first-note.treble.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION IN TWO PORTS (+2.264 -> -0.300 -> 0). OPENED as a pair with line-start.clef-to-first-note.bass -- the horizontal prefix defect that the page-crossing slur and tie residuals (system.slur-under-notes, system.tie-under-notes) name as sub-question 1, now isolated at its source and at natural length. A CLEF-ONLY line-start prefix (no key, no repeated time) binds its first note through Clef's (first-note . minimum-fixed-space . 5.0), the ONE break-align spring LilyPond measures from the left item's LEFT edge with a max: staff-spacing.cc:183-187 sets fixed = last_ext[LEFT] + std::max(last_ext.length(), distance), ideal = fixed. With the clef's own left edge at the column origin that is max(clef-width, 5.0) = 5.0, because every engraved clef is under 5 ss wide -- so the clef width is ABSORBED by the max, not added. Measured on 2.26.0: an interior system (clef-only) and an \omit-time single system both put the treble clef anchor at 0.8 and the first head at 5.8, a clef-to-head distance of 5.000000 EXACTLY, and the WIDER bass clef (ink 2.683 against 2.565) prints the IDENTICAL 5.000000 (line-start.clef-to-first-note.bass) -- the pair's cross-check. PREDICTION, written before the Lily# side was measured: Lily# double-counts the clef width (BreakAlignSpacing.FirstNoteSpring returns a bare (5.0, 5.0) that MultiStaffLayouter.cs:966-976 adds to a prefix width already ending at the clef's RIGHT ink), so residual = the clef's own ink width, ~+2.565 here and ~+2.683 for the bass twin, the two DIFFERING by the clef-width difference (~0.118). THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THE PAIR IS WHY THAT IS KNOWN: MEASURED, both twins read Lily# 7.264000000 for an IDENTICAL residual of +2.264000000. An equal residual on a treble and a wider bass clef FALSIFIES the per-clef-width double-count (that would differ by 0.118) and points instead to a FIXED +2.264 in Lily#'s clef-only prefix, width-INDEPENDENT -- the same shape of miss HANDOFF 5.2.1 records, where the pair disagreeing (or here, agreeing when a difference was predicted) is what exposes the true mechanism. CAUSE ISOLATED by instrumenting MultiStaffLayouter's line-start block (transient [PREFIX] dump on the interior systems): the clef-only case computes startX = CurrentIndent + prefixWidth with prefixWidth = the clef ink width (2.564 for treble), and springIdeal = the raw space-alist 5.0 (the FirstNoteSpring (5.0,5.0), unbumped -- s0.MinDistance is 0.2, so the Math.Max(min, s0.MinDistance) suspected earlier does NOT fire), so the first note lands at prefixWidth + 5.0 = clef-width + 5.0. That is the 5.0 measured from the clef's RIGHT ink (the prefix already reserved the whole clef width), where LilyPond's minimum-fixed-space measures it from the clef's LEFT ink with a max: note = last_ext[LEFT] + max(last_ext.length(), 5.0) = clef-left + 5.0, the 5.0 a TOTAL that ABSORBS the clef width rather than following it. So the clef width IS double-counted, exactly as first predicted -- what the prediction got wrong was the MEASUREMENT's behaviour, not the mechanism: the clef-anchor-to-note quantity reads clef-width-INDEPENDENT (+2.264 on both twins) because Lily#'s clef DRAW position co-varies with the clef width (its ink-left sits at clef-width - 2.264, so the width cancels in note-minus-clef-anchor). The residual still cleanly isolates this spring-frame defect at +2.264, relative to each side's own clef ink-left. Consistency check that the isolation is sound: Lily# draws the clef at 0.30 against LilyPond's 0.8 (a SEPARATE -0.5 left-edge-to-clef point, not this one), so the absolute first-note position differs by 2.264 - 0.5 = 1.76 -- exactly the ~1.76 ss system.slur-under-notes measured leaking through the bow under justification (Lily# first head 7.56 vs LilyPond 5.8). THE FIX (applied this session): BreakAlignSpacing.FirstNoteSpring now returns max(0, 5.0 - clefWidth) for the clef case, threading the same GClefWidth the prefix reserves, so the two cancel to max(width, 5.0) measured from the clef's LEFT ink -- the literal minimum-fixed-space arithmetic, NOT a baked constant. That put the first note at 5.000000 line-relative and this residual at -0.300000. THE SECOND PORT (defect-1, the missing left-edge-to-clef) closed the remaining -0.300000 to 0. Lily# reserved NO left-edge-to-clef space (its prefix started AT the clef, prefixWidth = clef width from 0) and drew the clef at an invented ClefGlyphXOffset of 0.30, where LilyPond seats the clef ink-left at 0.8 -- LeftEdge.space-alist (clef . (extra-space . 0.8)), LeftEdge extent (0 . 0) so the ideal is 0 + 0.8 (scm/define-grobs.scm:2091). Ported by making ClefGlyphXOffset 0.8 (its true LP value, no longer LILYSHARP-OWN -- one constant now read by DrawClef, SkylineBuilder AND CalculatePrefixWidth) and reserving it as the prefix's leading distance. That seats the clef ink-left at 0.8 and the note at 0.8 + max(clef-width, 5.0) - absorbed = 5.8, clef-to-note 5.000000 EXACTLY. The two ports together CLOSED sub-question 1: system.slur-under-notes -0.007709 -> +0.004203 (spring-frame) -> +0.000534 (left-edge-to-clef), and system.tie-under-notes -0.001883 -> +0.001469 -> +0.000442 -- both now at Pango-quantisation scale, the same named class as the slur's arc residual, not a defect. Twin sides differ in how they reach the clef-only prefix (LilyPond omits the meter on one system; Lily# reads an interior system, since it always draws a meter on system 0), verified equal -- the same documented harness asymmetry as the octave spelling.

line-start.clef-to-first-note.bass.why: CLOSED TO EXACT in two ports (+2.264 -> -0.300 -> 0), the mirror of line-start.clef-to-first-note.treble -- the SAME clef-only first-note spring bound by a WIDER clef. LilyPond prints the IDENTICAL 5.000000 (bass clef ink 2.683 is still under 5, so max(width, 5.0) = 5.0 absorbs it), the cross-check this pair exists for. PREDICTION: residual = the bass clef's ink width, ~+2.683, DIFFERENT from the treble twin's ~+2.565. MEASURED: +2.264000000, the SAME as the treble twin to nine digits -- the prediction was wrong because the prefix uses a FIXED GClefWidth for every clef, so both clefs read the identical value; the pair agreeing when a difference was predicted is what corrected the mechanism reading. FIXED identically to the treble twin (both went 7.264000 -> 4.700000 -> 5.000000, the pair holding at every stage, residual 0); the second port (left-edge-to-clef, ClefGlyphXOffset 0.3 -> 0.8) closed the -0.300000. Full account on line-start.clef-to-first-note.treble.

line-start.clef-to-time.treble.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.001000 -> 0), the TREBLE half of the defect-3 pair with line-start.clef-to-time.bass. On the first (metered) system the line-start meter binds to the clef through Clef.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.52)), measured off the clef's OWN ink right edge, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance rides on the clef ink width; the clef-ONLY clef->first-note does NOT show it (max(width, 5.0)-absorbed, width-independent). Measured on 2.26.0: clef anchor 0.8, time anchor 4.885, distance 4.085000. OPENED at residual -0.001000: Lily# read 4.084000 because GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returned the advance-derived GClefWidth (2.564) for the G clef rather than its stencil right edge; LilyPond reads the stencil ink (last_ext[RIGHT] = 2.565, break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142,242). THE FIX: LineStartClefWidth now returns ClefG.Right (2.565) for the treble family too, so every clef reads its own stencil ink exactly as LilyPond does -- no advance-vs-ink deviation left. MEASURED after the fix: Lily# 4.085000000, residual -0.000000000 EXACT. (The earlier decision to carry this -0.001 to spare treble snapshots a 0.001 re-space was reversed: byte-churn is not a reason to keep a non-faithful value. The re-space is sub-visual and mostly rounds away at 2-decimal SVG precision.)

line-start.clef-to-time.bass.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (-0.119400 -> 0). defect-3 was CalculatePrefixWidth reserving a FIXED GClefWidth for EVERY clef; the wider F clef (ink 2.6834 vs the treble G's 2.565) still got the treble G's width, so Lily# spaced the line-start meter as if the clef were a treble G. On a metered system the meter break-aligns to the clef through Clef.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.52)) measured off the clef's OWN ink right edge, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance rides on the clef ink width; the clef-ONLY clef->first-note does NOT show defect-3 (max(width, 5.0)-absorbed, width-independent, which is why line-start.clef-to-first-note.{treble,bass} read exact for BOTH clefs). Measured on 2.26.0: clef anchor 0.8, time anchor 5.0034, distance 4.203400 (= the treble control's 4.085 + 0.1184, exactly the ink-width difference 2.6834 - 2.5650). OPENED at residual -0.119400: Lily# printed 4.084000 for the bass, the SAME as the treble twin to the digit (the pair EQUAL where LilyPond DIFFERS -- the cross-check that this was exactly the fixed GClefWidth). THE FIX: GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returns the real per-clef stencil right edge -- ClefF.Right 2.6834 for bass/bass_8, ClefC.Right 2.720 for the C clefs -- and SpacingRules.MaxClefWidth threads the widest clef in the score through CalculatePrefixWidth AND FirstNoteSpring (the SAME width, so the clef-only case still cancels to max(width, 5.0)) AND SharedRenderer's DrawClef flow-anchor (so the drawn meter lands where the note was spaced from, and a grand staff's staves share ONE clef break-align column -- the wider bass F governs the treble staff's meter position too, keeping the two signatures aligned). Every clef -- INCLUDING the treble G (ClefG.Right 2.565, not the advance-derived 2.564) -- now reads its own stencil ink, so both DCT and DCB close to 0 with no advance-vs-ink deviation left (an earlier plan to keep G on the advance to spare treble snapshots a 0.001 re-space was reversed: byte-churn is not a reason to keep a non-faithful value). MEASURED after the fix: Lily# 4.203400000, residual -0.000000000 -- EXACT. Impact: bass/alto/C line-start meters and their metered first notes move ~0.12 right; treble meters move +0.001 (mostly rounds away at 2-decimal SVG precision); snapshots change wherever any clef appears (grand staves included).

note-to-note.quarter.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened, and opened to fill a hole rather than to chase a defect: every other point in this corpus measures FROM something -- barline.next.* from a bar line, line-start.* from the prefix -- so plain note-to-note spacing, the commonest distance on any page, had never been compared at all. Ragged (two measures, one system, which LilyPond and Lily# alike keep at natural width per constrained-breaking.cc:142-148), so this reads the spring's IDEAL and is paper-independent. Paired with note-to-note.eighth: the two differ by exactly the spacing-increment 1.2 on both sides, which is the cross-check -- a defect in the increment moves them apart, one in the base moves them together, and Lily# reproduces both. One pitch throughout so no stem-direction correction and no skyline nesting enters, leaving the duration space alone. WHY IT WAS OPENED: to test whether Lily#'s duration space explains justified.first-system.heads, the line breaker putting 4 bars on a system where LilyPond puts 5. It does not -- the ideals agree to nine digits. Together with the refuted esw hypothesis recorded on that entry, both the IDEAL and the MINIMUM are now eliminated as causes and the disagreement is in the breaker itself.

note-to-note.eighth.why: The eighth-note half of the note-to-note pair, exact from the start. Its value is note-to-note.quarter's less the spacing-increment 1.2 (2.504200 against 3.704200) on both sides; keeping both is what distinguishes a wrong increment from a wrong base. Note the quarter gap here is 3.704200, not score A's 3.002245: the common-shortest-duration of the piece is an eighth here and a quarter there, and the whole scale rides on it (spacing-spanner.cc calc_common_shortest_duration) -- the two probes agreeing on that is itself part of what these points check. Full account on note-to-note.quarter.

note-to-note.across-barline.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened (Lily# 3.772771429 against a LilyPond value recorded to six digits, so the 4.29e-7 is the rounding of the record and not a gap). The third of the plain note-to-note points, and the one that carries the BAR LINE: the two gaps inside a measure being exact leaves this one measuring what a bar line costs a line's total, which is the quantity a line breaker sums. Rendered on 2.26.0: last head of bar 1 at 23.506000, bar line ink 26.188771..26.378771, first head of bar 2 at 27.278771. It was opened to test whether the bar line explains justified.first-system.heads -- Lily# putting 4 bars on the first system where LilyPond puts 5. It does not. With the duration space, the note-to-note minimum, the line width, the three extra demerit terms and the DP's shape all eliminated before it, what is left is that the BREAKER's own per-measure spring totals may not equal the spacing the layout renders -- they are computed on a separate path (SystemBreaker.ComputeMultiStaffSpringData), and section 5.4's rule that the two spring systems and the break gate must agree is asserted for the springs but not for a line's TOTAL.

compressed.line-start.time-to-first-note.why: EXACT (the 4.63e-7 is the rounding of LilyPond's own six-place 3.694465). CLOSED 2026-07-25 by TWO things, and it needed both. (1) THE PAIR WAS MEASURING DIFFERENT MUSIC. This probe's Lily# side had the fixture's three phrases flattened into one melody block, and Lily# resets the relative frame at every phrase reference (Svg/Collector/RelativeResetMarker), so `slurs` opens on the c nearest C4 = c' in the fixture but continues the relative chain from the a that ends `ties` when inlined -- and the nearest c to a' is c''. Bars 4 to 8 were engraved an OCTAVE UP, which flips their stems DOWN, and that alone accounted for 0.314107 ss of natural width: the note-to-bar-line stem correction (note-spacing.cc:288-301 different_directions_correction, halved at :299-300) came out NEGATIVE where LilyPond's is positive (bar 4 measured -0.236707 against LilyPond's +0.236700 -- a clean sign flip), and a stem-DOWN first note after a bar line earns an optical correction that a stem-up one does not (staff-spacing.cc:55, `d == DOWN` only), widening the bar-line-to-first-note springs of bars 4 to 8 by 0.011 to 0.171. THE LESSON, because this was very nearly written up as a spacing defect: a Lily# probe source that INLINES a fixture's phrases is not that fixture's music. (2) THE COMPRESSIBILITY PORT. spring.cc:131-159's setters assign one field and call update_blocking_force only, so a note spring keeps the compressibility Spacing_spanner::note_spacing gave it, fraction * (duration_space - increment); Lily# had been rebuilding the spring through its defaulting constructor and getting ideal - min instead. With the pair fixed but the old compressibility this point would still read about -0.0007 (arithmetic from the measured overflow, not separately re-measured): the line's total compressibility is what converts the overflow into the solved force, and the line start gives up 0.8 * |force|. ALSO RETRACTED: the long-standing claim that 'the natural widths agree to 2e-5, decomposed column by column' per probes/ties-slurs-breaks-ragged.ly. That control omits the final bar line this score carries, so it too measured different music (its 101.907014 is exactly the real natural 102.807014 minus 0.900000), and with the final bar line in place LilyPond will not keep the eight bars on one ragged line at all. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and how to read LilyPond's springs at all (they are settable but not readable from Scheme): probes/compressed-line-force.ly engraves this music twice, ragged on a wide line (CLW) and justified (CLJ), so CLW - CLJ is |force| * inverse_compress_strength per spring and nothing else. LilyPond's natural 102.807014 against the 102.429921 line overflows by 0.377093 and solves force -0.006918750; dividing the per-spring yields by it gives 0.800000 at the line start, 1.698045 quarter-to-quarter, 2.898045 for a half and 0.400000 bar-line-to-note, summing to 54.701125. WHY THE POINT EXISTS: every other line-start point in this corpus is read at force 0, where Spring::length picks the STRETCH strength and neither the line start's fixed distance nor any compressibility is observable at all. Keep it. OLD MECHANISM NOTE, kept so it is not re-derived: the line start's own spring was never the disagreement -- both sides build ideal 2.000000 prefix-relative, min_distance 7.485000, compressibility 0.800000 (LineStartColumnTests.MeteredLineStart_SpringIsLilyPonds), and the 0.3 + min_dist floor of staff-spacing.cc:210-220 is what makes that 0.8 rather than 1.0. The fixture is test/ties-slurs, whose snapshot shares this regime.

note-to-note.half.why: EXACT from the moment it was opened, and opened to fill a hole the corpus did not know it had: every note-to-note point before this one was a QUARTER or an EIGHTH against a BLACK notehead. A half gap is not the quarter's plus the spacing-increment 1.2 -- it is 1.273200 more, because Note_spacing adds the LEFT column's head width and a half notehead is 1.377400 against the black head's 1.304200. So this point reads a glyph metric in the spacing path that nothing else does, and a defect in the half head's ink would move it while leaving every other note-to-note point exact. Measured 4.275445 on both sides; the same value falls out of the ties-slurs decomposition (probes/ties-slurs-breaks-ragged.ly, columns 23 to 24).

note-to-note.quarter-shortest.why: EXACT, and the PAIR against note-to-note.quarter: the same quarter-to-quarter gap, 3.002245 here against 3.704200 there, differing only in what the score's OTHER notes are. Spacing_spanner::find_shortest does not use the shortest note in the score; it takes the most common per-measure shortest and averages it with base-shortest-duration (1/8). NN's most common shortest IS 1/8, so its average is 1/8 again and the averaging is INVISIBLE there -- which means every duration-space point in this corpus was measured in the one regime where that step does nothing. Here the most common shortest is 1/4, global_shortest is 3/16, and a quarter's ratio is 4/3: (2 + log2 4/3) * 1.2 - 1.2 + 1.304200 = 3.002245. Lily# reproduces it to nine digits, so its port of the averaging is right and not merely untested. Section 5.2.1 item 4: exact is not the same as correct, but exact in a regime the corpus never entered is new information.

note-to-rest.half-rest.why: EXACT. Every rest point in this corpus measures a rest against a BAR LINE (F, barline.prev.whole-rest, barline.next.whole-rest); none has ever measured a note against a REST, i.e. a rest as the RIGHT-hand column of a spring. The prediction written before the measurement was that it equals note-to-note.quarter-shortest, since the space is decided by the LEFT column's duration and head width and the rest contributes only its left reach -- and it does, to six digits. That makes the point a guard rather than a discovery: a rest box that started paying its own way on the left would move this one and nothing else.

barline.prev.half-rest.why: EXACT. The closing side of the same measure, against barline.prev.whole-rest (5.598045) as the control: the two differ by exactly the rests' own ink, so the pair says the item-to-bar-line path reads the REST STENCIL's width and not a nominal box. GlyphMetrics.RestWidth / RestHeight are two of the unsourced nominal constants LpProvenanceTests still carries (handoff section 5.2.1 item 1), so this is the point that would catch them if the half rest's box were the nominal one.

justified.first-system.heads.why: CLOSED 2026-07-25 by 4bf72e9e (the break gate priced beamed notes with a flag) together with the removal of the invented OverfullPenalty -- both are needed, and neither alone moves it. The gate built its springs through a MeasureLayouter whose beam predicate was never set, so a beamed eighth took a skyline minimum of 2.532200 instead of 1.704200 and the merge_springs headroom (minimum + 0.3) lifted its IDEAL from LilyPond's 2.504200 to 2.832200 -- +0.984029 per bar of this music, so five bars needed 98.389000 where 95.844900 was available and the gate could not see LilyPond's five-bar first system as a natural fit. With the fix the gate reads LilyPond's own 18.693771 per bar, solves the five-bar line at force +0.0256 (stretched, as LilyPond's is) and cuts 5,5,6 -- but only once OverfullPenalty is gone, because the six-bar third line is compressed and the penalty priced it at 50000 x |force|. Measured (jn-line-forces.ly, JNN/JNJ). ⚠️ THE HYPOTHESIS RECORDED BELOW WAS WRONG, and is kept because being wrong in a stated direction is what made it testable: GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 makes the note-to-note minimum 0.2 too wide, which makes ideal - min SMALLER, the stretched line's force LARGER and a four-line solution look WORSE -- the opposite sign to the split actually seen. It is still an invention (handoff section 2H) and still wants removing; it was simply not this. PREVIOUS TEXT: OPEN. How many notes the LINE BREAKER puts on the first system of a justified score: LilyPond 5 bars (30 heads), Lily# 4 (24). This was opened as the precondition for a justified note-to-note pair -- on a justified line the slack is shared in proportion to inverse_stretch_strength = ideal - min, so the note-to-note MINIMUM is finally observable (every other point in this corpus is ragged-right, i.e. at force 0, where minima are never consulted) -- and it immediately caught the two engravers laying the music out differently. The gap points that were to sit beside it were held back: with 4 bars sharing the width LilyPond gives 5, Lily#'s first-system gaps read 4.909926 and 3.107063 against 3.765697 and 2.534949, and recording those as note-to-note residuals would attribute a line-breaking disagreement to note spacing -- the exact shape section 5.2 forbids. HYPOTHESIS to test when this is worked, not a claim: Lily#'s note-to-note minimum is 0.2 too wide (GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 standing in for the boxes' extra-spacing-width, probe N2N: LilyPond's column distance for two same-pitch quarter heads is 1.504200 where Lily# computes 1.704200), and since inverse_stretch_strength is ideal - min, too large a minimum means too little stretchability, which is exactly the input the breaker's force and demerits are computed from. If so this point closes together with that fix rather than needing one of its own. Measured on the DEFAULT page on both sides -- LilyPond's A4 with 10mm margins is 102.429921 to the final bar line, LayoutOptions.Default 102.429925 -- since unlike every other point here a justified one is paper-dependent.

justified.note-to-note.quarter.why: SEEDED 2026-07-25, the moment justified.first-system.heads went exact and the two engravers finally put the same five bars on this system. The quarter gap on a JUSTIFIED line, read from the same JN dump that gives the head count: `bar= 1 n=30 first= 8.585000 quarter 3.765697 eighth 2.534949`. Its ragged twin note-to-note.quarter is exact at 3.704200, so this point sees only what justification adds. It opened EXACT (+5.3e-8, with the eighth at -4.7e-7 — Pango-quantisation scale), which is a result worth recording for what it REFUTES. ⚠️ PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND WRONG: that this pair would be the ledger key for removing GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4, on the reasoning that a justified line shares slack in proportion to inverse_stretch_strength = ideal - min and so is the first point here that can see a spring's MINIMUM. It cannot. LilyPond's own note_spacing sets `inverse_stretch_strength = fraction * max (0.1, len - min)` with min = the spacing INCREMENT, not the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc; SpacingRules.CreateSpring carries the same REF), so a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum at all and MinItemGap is invisible in this regime. The knob binds only where a spring is compressed ONTO its minimum, so the key that removal needs is a COMPRESSED note-to-note point, which this corpus still does not have. What this pair does pin is that justification itself is exact once both sides break alike.

justified.note-to-note.eighth.why: The eighth gap of the same justified line, from the same dump, and the pair with justified.note-to-note.quarter: both springs stretch on ONE solved force, so their residuals must move together. Both opened exact (-4.7e-7 here, +5.3e-8 there). The eighth is the more sensitive of the two — its ideal is smaller, so any error in a spring's stretchability is a larger share of it — which is why both were recorded rather than one, and why their agreeing at 1e-7 is what says the stretch model is right rather than cancelling. See justified.note-to-note.quarter for the prediction this pair REFUTED (that it would be the key for GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4: a stretched line never consults the skyline minimum, so that knob is invisible here and its key must be a COMPRESSED point).

compressed.note-to-note.quarter.why: CLOSED the day it opened, by the port it was opened for: GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 is gone from the note-to-note path and the gap is built the way LilyPond builds it -- each grob's extra-spacing-width folded into its own spacing box (separation-item.cc:166-179), the spring minimum taken as the padding-free skyline distance with skyline-vertical-padding 0.08 (note-spacing.cc:78-83), and the ROD as that distance plus the spacing spanner's padding 0.1 (spacing-spanner.cc:315-316 into separation-item.cc:56). Lily# now reads 1.604200000 against LilyPond's 1.604200. The invented knob was 0.4 of gap on 1.304200 of ink; the port is 0.1 + (0.1 + 1.304200 + 0.1), which is the same number reached from LilyPond's own two steps instead of one made-up one. HISTORY, kept because it is how the point came to be right: The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until the ROD binds, which is the only regime in which that floor is observable. ⚠️ FIRST MEASURED WRONG, and the correction is the point: with middle C as the pitch LilyPond read 1.956300, and that is not the head-to-head minimum at all -- c' in a treble staff carries a LEDGER LINE, a ledger sticks out past the head on both sides, and it joins the column's horizontal-skylines like any other ink. The probe was measuring the unported ledger geometry (handoff section 2E) on top of the minimum. On g', which sits on a staff line and has no ledger, LilyPond saturates at 1.604200 -- exactly the rod probe N2N records -- for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, and the dumped rods on every column read 1.604200 to the digit. The entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside that plateau. SEEDED 2026-07-25. The note-to-note gap of a line squeezed until every spring sits on its MINIMUM -- the only regime in which a spring minimum is observable, and therefore the ledger key that removing GlyphMetrics.MinItemGap 0.4 has to move. Ragged points read ideals at force 0; the justified pair reads a stretched line, whose inverse_stretch_strength LilyPond builds from the spacing INCREMENT and not from the skyline minimum (lily/spacing-basic.cc), which is why both of those opened exact and neither can see this. MEASURED: LilyPond's gap for this bar falls 3.048125 -> 2.037936 as the line narrows and then STOPS at 1.956300 for every width from 19.916929 down to 12.519213, so the entry is read at 30mm (17.071654 ss), inside the plateau. ⚠️ PREDICTION WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND WRONG: that it would saturate at the ROD, 1.604200, measured on probe N2N as the hard floor under the spring minimum 1.504200. It saturates 0.352100 above that, so the floor that actually binds a compressed line is NOT the rod N2N reads, and what sets it is not yet identified -- that is the open question this entry carries, and it must be answered before MinItemGap is touched, because a port aimed at 1.604200 would be aimed at the wrong number.

staff.tab-pair.staff-staff-inside.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. WHAT UNIT A STAFF-TO-STAFF DISTANCE IS IN when the lower staff is a TAB staff. LilyPond's TabStaff sets StaffSymbol.staff-space = 1.5 for every string count (ly/engraver-init.ly), so a six-string tab staff's LINES span (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 against a notation staff's 4.000000 -- pinned exact by tab.staff.line-span.six-string. The open question was what that does to the DISTANCE above it, and the two candidate answers were nearly a factor of two apart: (a) Align_interface works between VerticalAxisGroup REFERENCE POINTS and staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance is in the PAGE's staff spaces, so the refpoint distance is 9.000000 whatever the lines do; or (b) the distance is measured from the staff's EDGES or in its own space, and a taller staff pushes the pair apart. PREDICTION, written before running: (a), 9.000000 to six digits, with staff.notation-pair.staff-staff-inside as the control. FALSIFIER: 10.750000 = 9 + (7.5 - 4)/2, which would mean LilyPond spaces from the edges and Lily#'s nominal-height arithmetic is accidentally right. THE PREDICTION HELD: measured 9.000000 on both books, and the two are equal to the digit, so the tab staff's extra 3.5 staff spaces of lines change the distance by nothing. ⚠️ THE FLOOR DOES NOT BIND, which is what makes this a reading of the SPEC rather than of the ink: both books came back at exactly the basic-distance rather than above it (the dump also reports the tab staff's own ink below its refpoint as 3.800000 = 7.6/2, i.e. the 7.5 span widened by half a line thickness at each edge and centred on the middle line -- the refpoint really is staff position 0). ⇒ THE FORK TOOK BRANCH (a), so the island is real: Lily# subtracts a flat nominal 4.000000 for the pair's span (MultiStaffLayouter.GapSpan, gated by IsSpecSpacedRowBoundary so only a text-row boundary takes the refpoint frame), which puts a tab pair's refpoints at 9 + (7.5 - 4)/2 = 10.750000. ⚠️ MEASURED PRICE OF THE FIX: removing that gate moves 20 snapshots -- 17 tab and 3 ossia -- which is the '~20 snapshots' HANDOFF has attached to this island for several sessions. THIS ENTRY IS THE KEY THAT JUSTIFIES THAT REBASE (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (3)); it did not exist before, which is why the island kept being deferred. ⚠️ Keep staff.notation-pair.staff-staff-inside exact while this closes, or the fix moved the wrong thing. ---- CLOSED THE SAME DAY, by the port it was opened for: MultiStaffLayouter.GapSpan asks RefpointSpanToGap for EVERY group boundary now instead of only where a text row is involved, and IsSpecSpacedRowBoundary -- the gate that selected between the two frames -- is gone with it. 9.000000 on both sides, and the control did not move. THE 20 SNAPSHOTS MOVED and are approved against this entry. ⚠️ AN OSSIA PAIR IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS and must not be read as if it were: its span is right now, but the caller still multiplies the gap by OssiaScaleFactor, which LilyPond has no counterpart for -- book OSSD (added the same day, an ossia-sized staff under an ordinary one) reads 9.000000 exactly like this one and like the notation control, so LilyPond scales the STAFF and not the distance. That leaves an ossia pair short by the scale alone, and it is a separate named quantity. ⚠️ OSSD IS NOT YET A LEDGER PAIR: it puts the small staff BELOW, while Lily#'s `ossia` renders ABOVE the staff it decorates, so the two sides are not the same arrangement (HANDOFF 5.0, traps 5 and 6). The ossia entry wants a book with the small staff above; what OSSD establishes is the LilyPond FACT that the distance is unscaled.

page.tab-only.first-staff-refpoint.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. WHERE A TAB STAFF SITS ON THE PAGE, which is the question staff.tab-pair.staff-staff-inside asked one frame in. That entry measured a distance BETWEEN two staves of one system and found it 9.000000 whatever the lower staff's line span is; this one measures the PAGE's own anchor against a staff that is not four staff spaces tall. Book TABL is ONE six-string tab staff and many systems, so every distance in it is the page's and none of it is Align_interface's. WHY THE QUANTITY EXISTS AT ALL: a six-string tab staff's lines span (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 (tab.staff.line-span.six-string), so its refpoint -- staff position 0, the middle of the span -- sits 3.750000 below its top line where an ordinary staff's sits 2.000000 below, and every LilyPond page anchor is written against that refpoint. No other entry in this corpus reads a page anchor over a staff of any height but 4.000000. PREDICTION, written before running (it is in the .ly header): 11.690551 = top-margin 5.690551 + top-system-spacing's basic-distance 6.000000, identical to the notation control NTL, because the floor loses -- a tab system carries 3.800000 of ink above its refpoint and 3.800000 + padding 1 = 4.800000 < 6. THE PREDICTION HELD on LilyPond's side: TABL and NTL both read 11.690551 to six digits, so LilyPond puts the first staff of a tab page exactly where it puts the first staff of a notation page. ⇒ THE FORK TOOK THE BRANCH THAT MAKES THE ISLAND REAL. Lily# reads 13.440551000, a residual of exactly +1.750000000 = 3.750000 - 2.000000, and the cause is one term: LayoutUtilities.CalculateFirstSystemY converts from the refpoint frame LilyPond's top spring is written in back into Lily#'s own system-origin frame by subtracting `_options.StaffHeight / 2.0` -- a NOMINAL half staff, 2.000000 for every staff there is. ⚠️ THE DISTANCE IS RIGHT AND THE ANCHOR IS WRONG, which is why the book carries two readings: system.tab-only.natural-distance is exact at 12.000000 on this same page. A fix that moves the gap has moved the wrong thing. ⚠️ DO NOT CLOSE IT BY SPECIAL-CASING TAB: the defect is the frame conversion, and the same nominal 4.000000 is assumed by SkylineBuilder.BuildSystemSkylines, which seeds notes, beams and clef about a derived -staffHeight/2 while seeding the staff LINES at the placed span (HANDOFF's item 4). THIS ENTRY IS THE KEY THAT JUSTIFIES MOVING THAT ISLAND'S SNAPSHOTS; it did not exist before, which is why the island kept being deferred. ⚠️ AND IT CORRECTS THE ISLAND'S FRAMING, measured in the same dump: HANDOFF asked for 'a point that measures at what height a tab staff's notes and clef enter the system silhouette', and the answer is that they do not enter it. TABL's ink below its last refpoint is 3.800000 EXACTLY -- the outermost string line (7.6/2) and nothing further -- and the TAB clef's own ink about the refpoint is [-2.880000, 2.880000], well INSIDE the lines. A tab system's silhouette IS its staff symbol on LilyPond's side, so seeding those grobs at their placed offset changes the silhouette by nothing; what the placed offset changes is this anchor. ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL IS TWO TERMS, and they were separated the same day by perturbation (both perturbations reverted -- no port has shipped). ⑴ Taking the half staff from the PLACED first staff instead of `_options.StaffHeight / 2.0` moves this reading 1.750000 -> 0.550000 and MOVES NO SNAPSHOT AT ALL. ⑵ The remaining 0.550000 is the silhouette half and it is item (4) itself: Lily#'s up-extent for this system is 1.800000 because SeedClef anchors the clef about the nominal middle line at -2.000000, so the top spring's floor comes to 1.800000 + 3.750000 + padding 1 = 6.550000 and BINDS, where LilyPond's 3.800000 + 1 = 4.800000 loses to the basic-distance 6. (LilyPond's tab clef is also a different glyph -- its ink is [-2.880000, 2.880000] about the refpoint against the treble clef's [-3.550000, 3.800000] -- so the clef Lily# seeds on a tab staff is not the one LilyPond draws either.) ⇒ ONE NUMBER, TWO PORTS, and it only reaches 0 when both land. ⚠️ THE '22 SNAPSHOTS' HANDOFF ATTACHES TO THIS ISLAND DO NOT ATTACH TO THIS QUANTITY: the anchor conversion moves none of them. What the same perturbation DID break is the SELECTION -- generalising PageLayouter.SprungStaffOffsets to 'the outer staves as placed' regressed hara-kiri.wide-ink.lone-staff-to-next-system by -2.000000 (it picked a HIDDEN staff) and took four lyrics.hara-kiri.grouper.* entries with it. That is the measured form of 'the selection has to skip text rows and hara-kiri'd staves', and it is the real blocker, not a snapshot price. ⚠️ THREE HOMES compute this half staff -- LayoutEngine.Layout (the first system's Y), LayoutEngine.CreatePages (the single-page path, which is the one this book's default paper takes), and PageLayouter (the optimal-paging path) -- and which is live depends on the paper regime. The first perturbation was spent on one that is not (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (2): the same quantity written three times is three models). ---- CLOSED THE SAME DAY, by the port it was opened for: 11.690551 to nine digits, residual 0.000000000, with all three controls unmoved. The three homes are one, LayoutEngine.PageAnchorOffsets, which reads the placed refpoint of the first (last) SPACEABLE staff through the same ClassifySystem selection the loose chain uses; SkylineBuilder seeds the silhouette's staff at the middle of its OWN placed span; and PageLayouter.SprungStaffOffsets -- whose `return (0, 0)` for a system with no staff springs was the branch keeping the old arithmetic -- is gone. ⚠️ BOTH TERMS WERE NEEDED, exactly as predicted above: the anchor alone leaves 0.550000 (the clef, seeded about a nominal middle line, raises the top spring's floor to 6.550000 and it binds), and the clef alone leaves 1.200000. ⚠️ MEASURED PRICE: 22 snapshots -- 19 tab and 3 ossia -- all of them the CONTENT-SIZED page's height and a uniform shift with it (a tab page is 0.250000 to 1.750000 shorter, an ossia page 6.190000, because the band over-reserved above the first spaceable staff). No corpus entry other than this one moved, and the tab/ossia drawn geometry inside a system is unchanged (checked with png --crop on test/tab-with-chords: identical). ⚠️ TWO THINGS THIS DID NOT CLOSE, both named in the code: (a) the silhouette still takes the outermost ELEMENT rather than the outermost spaceable staff, so a system whose outer element is a text row still puts no staff in its own skyline -- changing that alone drops book LYRHKG's inter-system floor from 8.900000 to 1.707200 (the lyric rows Lily# keeps OUT of the skyline were standing in for the staff kept out with them; the two exclusions are ONE quantity and no point measures either); (b) the page BREAKER keeps the nominal refpoint extent, because moving it re-breaks pages and no point measures a page count over a staff that is not four staff spaces tall.

system.tab-only.natural-distance.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28, exact on both sides, and deliberately not a spare. It is the SECOND reading of book TABL and the one that says the tab defect is an ANCHOR rather than a DISTANCE: page.tab-only.first-staff-refpoint is 1.750000 out on this very page while this is 12.000000 to the digit. PREDICTION, written before running: 12.000000, system-system-spacing's basic-distance, because that floor loses too -- 3.800000 of ink below one system's refpoint plus 3.800000 above the next plus padding 1 = 8.600000 < 12. It held on both engravers. ⚠️ THE CONTROL SHOWS THE INK IS NOT BEING MEASURED HERE: NTL is the same music on the same paper with an ordinary staff, its ink below the refpoint is 5.045000 rather than 3.800000 (the low g and a on their ledger lines), and it reads the same 12.000000. ⚠️ AN EXACT POINT THAT HAS TO STAY EXACT -- the port that closes the first-refpoint entry must not move this one (HANDOFF 5.3: a point that is blind to a defect is still a net for the fix).

page.tab-only.staves-on-first-page.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. The structural guard for the two TABL readings (HANDOFF 5.0, trap 8): both of them return a plausible number off a page that holds a different number of systems -- the refpoint one reads the topmost staff whatever it is, and the gap one reads whatever gaps a page happens to have uniformly. 24 bars of tab land 3 systems on one page on both engravers. ⚠️ A count is not a distance and does not enter the ss total (unit).

page.tab-control.first-staff-refpoint.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. THE CONTROL for page.tab-only.first-staff-refpoint, carried rather than assumed. Book NTL is TABL's part on TABL's paper with the staff spelled as an ordinary Staff -- the pair differs in one word -- so 'the tab reading is off' cannot be confused with 'this whole arrangement is off'. It is deliberately NOT book L, which reads the same quantity but on different music and different paper. MEASURED 11.690551 on both engravers and identical to TABL's LilyPond side: LilyPond's page anchor does not know how tall the staff under it is. ⚠️ AND THE INK DIFFERS A GREAT DEAL WHILE THE ANCHOR DOES NOT -- NTL's notes hang below the staff on ledger lines (5.045000 of ink below the refpoint against TABL's 3.800000) and both books still land on top-system-spacing's basic-distance, which is what makes this a reading of the SPEC.

system.tab-control.natural-distance.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. THE CONTROL for system.tab-only.natural-distance -- the same music and paper with a notation staff. 12.000000 on both engravers and equal to TABL's reading to the digit, so a six-string tab staff's extra 3.5 staff spaces of lines change the distance between systems by nothing, exactly as they change the distance between two staves of one system by nothing (staff.tab-pair.staff-staff-inside).

page.tab-control.staves-on-first-page.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. The count for the NTL readings, for the reason page.tab-only.staves-on-first-page carries one. That both books break 24 bars into the same 3 systems is also what makes the pair a pair: had the tab staff broken differently, the two would be spacing pages of different shapes and the identity between them would say nothing.

staff.notation-pair.staff-staff-inside.why: THE CONTROL half of the tab staff-spacing pair (book NST). The same music on the same paper with the lower staff spelled as an ordinary Staff instead of a TabStaff, so it is the same two elements of one VerticalAlignment and the same staff-staff-spacing. It is exact on both sides from the moment it was opened, which is the point: a control that is already exact while the tab half is 1.750000 wide proves the defect is the SPAN Lily# subtracts and not the arrangement, the pitches, or the page. ⚠️ Keep it pinned when the nominal-height span goes: it must stay exact while the tab half closes.

staff.ossia-pair.staff-staff-inside.why: OPENED AND CLOSED 2026-07-28 (-1.636081 -> 0). THE OSSIA DISTANCE ITSELF -- the last named invention of the tab/ossia frame island, and the one quantity that island had left once door (3) fixed the SPAN (13de8545) and door (4) fixed the page ANCHOR (0a2b4e5d). Lily# multiplies the whole inter-group gap by OssiaScaleFactor = magstep(-3) (MultiStaffLayouter.cs, three sites: CalculateSystemHeight, LayoutStaffGroups, LayoutStaffGroupsWithSkylines), i.e. it shrinks the DISTANCE along with the staff. LilyPond does not: books OSSD (small staff BELOW), OSSU (small staff ABOVE, the arrangement Lily# actually renders) and TABS (a tab staff below) all read 9.000000 -- three different arrangements, one number, so the distance does not know what it is spacing. The falsifier 9 * magstep(-3) = 6.363961 did not fire on any of them. ⚠️ WHY THIS COULD NOT BE OPENED BEFORE, AND WHY THAT REASON WAS WRONG: the entry was held back on a reported Lily# DRAWING defect -- 'an ossia spanning every measure draws its staff lines at the system origin with unscaled 1.000000 spacing and a width of 135.55 on a 119.50 page'. Measured again through RecordingDocumentContext (which composes the group transform) the drawing is CORRECT: lines at 6.158232..8.986632, staff space 0.707100, width 95.844921 on a page 119.501575 wide. 135.55 is that same width read INSIDE the ossia's scale group -- 95.844921 / 0.7071 = 135.546, six digits -- and 'the system origin' and 'unscaled 1.000000' are the same group-local frame (SharedRenderer.cs:445 draws an ossia's content at localStaffY = pageHeight and the group transform puts it in place). ⇒ There was no drawing defect and no need for a fragment-shaped pair; the blocker was a reading. PREDICTION, written before the port: dropping the three multiplications lands this on 9.000000 EXACTLY, with nothing else to change. It is derived and not fitted -- the drawn gap between the ossia's bottom line and the staff's top line is 3.949719, and 9 - (2.000000 + 2 * 0.707100) = 5.585786 is what StaffGap returns before the scale, 5.585786 * 0.7071 = 3.949719 to six digits. So the refpoint distance after the port is 3.949719 / 0.7071 + 1.414200 + 2.000000 = 9.000000. FALSIFIER: any other landing means the gap the scale is applied to is not the one this arithmetic names, and the remaining amount is a SECOND quantity -- most likely the span, which would mean 13de8545 did not reach this path. ⇒ ★ THE PREDICTION HELD TO THE DIGIT: 9.000000000, residual 0.000000000, and the control did not move. The falsifier did not fire, so the span 13de8545 fixed does reach this path and the scale really was the only quantity left. All three multiplications went together -- which one is live changes with the paper regime (HANDOFF 5.2.1(2), the three homes of the nominal half staff), so removing one would have closed this on some papers and not others. PRICE: three snapshots, test/ossia + test/ossia-key + test/ossia-beams, each moving its ossia 1.636081 further from its staff with the page height and every other grob unchanged. ⚠️ A LITERAL 9 WOULD PASS THIS ENTRY, so the rule is asserted separately: LpGeometryLedgerTests.AnOssiaPair_IsSpacedByTheSpec_NotByTheOssiasOwnScale drives the spec's basic-distance to 9 and 14 and requires the pair to follow with coefficient 1 and to stay equal to its control. The scaled implementation fails it at both (14 lands at 10.899419, the 0.7071 fingerprint) -- demonstrated before the fix, not assumed. ⚠️ THE SPRINGS ARE THE SAME ISLAND AND ARE STILL OPEN: MultiStaffLayouter.StaffSprings skips an ossia pair. The reason it gave -- 'closing that needs the ossia distance itself ported first' -- is now spent, and the pair sits ON the spec so a spring built from it is at its own ideal. What is NOT measured is the page-level consequence: an ossia is spaceable in LilyPond and widens staff-refpoint-extent (book LYROS reads 18.000000 against Lily#'s two-staff span). That span needs a point before the skip goes.

staff.ossia-control.staff-staff-inside.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. THE CONTROL half of the ossia pair (book OSSUN). The same part twice on the same paper with the upper one spelled as an ordinary staff instead of an ossia, so the two halves differ in ONE WORD and that word is the measurement. LilyPond's own two books are an IDENTITY -- OSSU and OSSUN both read 9.000000 to the digit, because magstep scales the staff and Align_interface accumulates between VerticalAxisGroup reference points -- so whatever difference Lily# shows between its two halves is entirely its own (HANDOFF 5.0: the strongest pair is the one LilyPond reads as an identity). It is exact from the moment it was opened, which is the point: an ordinary pair already lands on staff-staff-spacing's basic-distance while the ossia half sits 1.636081 below it, so the defect is the SCALE and not the arrangement, the pitches, the nesting or the page. ⚠️ Keep it pinned while the scale goes: it must stay exact while the ossia half closes, and a port that moved BOTH would be changing the pair's spacing rather than the ossia's.

staff.ossia-pair.compressed.staff-staff-.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. THE OSSIA PAIR ON A PAGE THAT MUST SQUEEZE -- the regime staff.ossia-pair.staff-staff-inside cannot reach. That entry reads the distance at REST, where a RIGID pair and a SOLVED one are both 9.000000, so it is blind to MultiStaffLayouter.StaffSprings skipping an ossia pair outright; perturbing that skip on 2026-07-28 moved nothing anywhere in the corpus, because every ossia book in it is a single content-sized page at force 0 (HANDOFF 5.3: perturbed-and-nothing-moved can be a regime rather than a death). LILYPOND, MEASURED: 8.787816 on page 1, i.e. its ideal 9 less one force, and the falsifier is inside the same dump -- (9 - 8.787816) / 1 = 0.212184 equals (12 - 11.151264) / 4 = 0.212184 to six digits, one force for the page rather than two unrelated numbers. So an ossia's distance IS an ordinary staff spring in LilyPond's chain: an ossia is a `\new Staff`, its VerticalAxisGroup prints aff=() (spaceable) in the same dump, and page-layout-problem springs every consecutive spaceable pair. ⚠️ THE COMPRESS STRENGTH IS 1, NOT JSK'S 2, and that is the SPEC and not the regime: Axis_group_interface::calc_maybe_pure_staff_staff_spacing (axis-group-interface.cc:1007-1027) returns StaffGrouper.staff-staff-spacing (minimum 7, define-grobs.scm:3352-3355) when a staff-grouper exists -- JSK is a PianoStaff -- and otherwise falls through to the VerticalAxisGroup's own default-staff-staff-spacing (minimum 8, no stretchability, :4237-4239). An ossia is a bare Staff, so it takes the fall-through. PREDICTION, written before Lily# is measured: 9.000000 EXACTLY, because a rigid pair prints its ideal whatever force the page solves, giving residual +0.212184 = one force x strength 1. FALSIFIER: any other reading. Below 9 means something OTHER than the skip is deciding this distance (an alignment minimum, or a second path) and that has to be dumped before the skip is touched; above 9 means the ink binds and the book is measuring a floor rather than a spring -- the alignment minimum here is the ossia's scaled clef 2.510179 + the staff's 3.800000 + padding 1 = 7.310179, well clear. ⚠️ THIS ENTRY DOES NOT CLOSE BY DELETING THE SKIP. Lily# puts this book's first staff 3.884 too far DOWN the page, and the page then compresses everything below it to compensate, which is what the two gap entries are reading. ⇒ ★ ONE ADDRESS, FOUR SYMPTOMS. ⚠️ And it is not the ossia's: this book has no ossia in it. ★★ CORRECTED THE SAME SESSION, AND THE ADDRESS WAS THE PROBE ITSELF: the 3.884000 was a SECTION MARK that only the Lily# half engraved (`form main { A }` prints one; the .ly half has no header, title or markup by design). It did not move with the page in any regime -- compressed, stretched and a one-system page all read 14.350551 -- which is what a fixed reservation looks like and what a spring never does; that invariance is what exposed it. Spelled `~A` the reading is 10.490551, residual +0.024000, and THAT is the real term: Lily# rests on its top floor 3.800000 + 1 = 4.800000 where LilyPond compresses the top spring past it to 4.776000. ⇒ ★ THE LESSON IS OLDER THAN THE FINDING (HANDOFF 5.0): a pair's two sides must be the SAME MUSIC, and a header on one side only is the same trap as a missing final barline or a flattened phrase. ★★ MEASURED AGAIN 2026-07-28 (session 25) AND THE +0.024000 IS A GLYPH METRIC, isolated by perturbation rather than by arithmetic over two readings. Lily#'s top spring on this book is BLOCKED AT ITS FLOOR: the head reads exactly 4.800000 below the top margin, while the force this page solves (0.214493) would put it at 6 + f x 6 = 4.713045, so what is being read is the floor and not the solve. Perturbing GlyphMetricsGenerated.ClefG's bbox TOP moves that floor one for one (4.800000 -> 4.850000 at Top 4.850000, both pages still compressed at f = 0.215881), so the floor IS ClefG.Top and nothing else is up there: the treble clef's origin sits on the G line one staff space below the middle, so its ink above the middle is Top - 1.0 = 3.800000, plus top-system-spacing's padding 1. LilyPond is at ITS floor by the same argument -- 4.776000 is neither the ideal 6 nor 6 + f x 6 = 4.718712 at its own force 0.213548 -- so LilyPond's clef reaches 3.776000 above the middle line where LILC gives 3.800000. ⚠️ THE 0.024000 IS NOT THE KNOWN CLEF SLIVER: that family (page.clef.first-staff-refpoint, system.clef-bounded-distance) runs 4e-5 to 8.3e-4 and this is three hundred times bigger, and it is not a uniform scale error either -- the SAME glyph's downward reach agrees with LilyPond to 8e-5 on book S. What it needs is LilyPond instrumented for what a Clef's vertical-skylines takes as its top (HANDOFF 2C), NOT a constant chosen to fit. ★★ MOVED BY THE GLYPH-SKYLINE PORT 2026-07-28: a grob whose vertical-skylines come from its STENCIL is spaced by the glyph's OUTLINE, not by the designed LILC box its extent is (scm/define-grobs.scm:902 Clef and :35 Accidental, against lily/grob.cc:85-89 simple_vertical_skylines_from_extents which NoteHead:2595 falls back to). The two boxes differ by 0.024 above and 0.010 below on the G clef, 0.448 below on the F clef. EXACT. The +0.024000 was the clef's upward slack: the floor is the outline's 3.776000.

page.ossia-control.compressed.last-staff.why: SEEDED 2026-07-28. The control's foot of chain, identical to the ossia half's on LilyPond's side (10.230551 on both). Carried so that the two ends and the two gaps together make the page's force attributable rather than leaving four residuals to be read as four defects (HANDOFF 5.3). ★ MEASURED: 10.240551, residual +0.010000 -- the foot is very nearly right, which is exactly what makes the HEAD the address rather than the chain as a whole. ★★ AND THE +0.010000 HAS AN ADDRESS TOO (2026-07-28, session 25): it is the CLEF, the same object the head's +0.024000 is. This foot sits on its floor, which is last-bottom-spacing's padding 1 plus the ink below the last staff's refpoint, and that ink is the treble clef's downward reach: 1.000000 + 3.550000 = 4.550000, against LilyPond's 4.540000 (both read from the bottom margin 5.690551). Perturbing GlyphMetricsGenerated.ClefG's bbox BOTTOM by 0.050000 moves this reading by exactly 0.050000 and leaves the control's HEAD untouched, so the two ends are floored by the two ends of one glyph box and neither is a spring. ⇒ Lily#'s LILC box for clefs.G is WIDER THAN LILYPOND'S STENCIL AT BOTH ENDS -- 0.024000 above the middle line and 0.010000 below -- and the slack is ASYMMETRIC, so it is not a scale factor. ⚠️ It is not the 0.27% effective-scale question either: 0.27% of 3.550000 is 0.009570 and would account for the bottom, but 0.27% of 4.800000 is 0.012960 against the 0.024000 actually measured at the top. ⇒ ONE OBJECT, TWO NUMBERS, and four ledger residuals on these two books reduce to them. Chasing it means dumping what LilyPond takes as a Clef's stencil extent (HANDOFF 2C), not adjusting a bbox to fit. ★★ MOVED BY THE GLYPH-SKYLINE PORT 2026-07-28: a grob whose vertical-skylines come from its STENCIL is spaced by the glyph's OUTLINE, not by the designed LILC box its extent is (scm/define-grobs.scm:902 Clef and :35 Accidental, against lily/grob.cc:85-89 simple_vertical_skylines_from_extents which NoteHead:2595 falls back to). The two boxes differ by 0.024 above and 0.010 below on the G clef, 0.448 below on the F clef. EXACT. The same 0.010000 as its ossia twin.

tab.staff.line-span.six-string.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (-1.000000 -> 0). The DEFECT half of the tab string-spacing pair, against tab.staff.line-span.four-string as CONTROL. LilyPond's TabStaff sets StaffSymbol.staff-space = 1.5 for EVERY string count (ly/engraver-init.ly), so a six-string tab staff spans (6-1) * 1.5 = 7.500000 line centre to line centre; measured on 2.26.0 as staffY -7.600000..0.000000, the 7.6 being that 7.5 widened by half a line thickness at each edge (probe line-start-mindist.ly score CGT). Lily# instead TAPERS the spacing by string count -- EngravingDefaults.TabStringSpace returns 1.5 below five strings, 1.4 at five and 1.3 at six -- so it spans 5 * 1.3 = 6.500000, a full staff space short. The stated reason for the taper is that a five- or six-string staff should not grow too tall, which is a Lily# aesthetic judgement and not a LilyPond quantity; it also works AGAINST Lily#'s own (ratified, HANDOFF section 3) larger fret digits, whose 1.7875 height already overlaps a 1.3 string gap and is what the white occluding background exists to hide. The control lands on 1.5 by accident -- Lily#'s taper happens to agree with LilyPond below five strings -- which is what isolates the taper rather than the tab staff as a whole. THE FIX: TabStringSpace returns 1.5 for every string count, LilyPond's one value; the parameter is kept and deliberately unused so each call site says the spacing does not depend on it. MEASURED after: Lily# 7.500000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT, with the four-string control unmoved at 0 -- the fix moved the taper and nothing else. Impact: five- and six-string tab staves grow (a six-string staff 6.5 -> 7.5 tall), which also gives the deliberately larger fret digits more room; every five- or six-string tab snapshot re-bases.

tab.staff.line-span.four-string.why: The CONTROL half of the tab string-spacing pair. A four-string tab staff spans (4-1) * 1.5 = 4.500000 on both sides -- LilyPond by its one staff-space of 1.5, Lily# because EngravingDefaults.TabStringSpace's taper happens to return 1.5 below five strings. It is exact from the moment it was opened, which is the point: a control that is already exact while the six-string half is 1.000000 short proves the defect is the TAPER and not the tab staff's geometry generally. Measured on 2.26.0: space=1.500000 lines=4 staffY=-5.192000..-0.592000, a 4.6 extent over the 4.5 span (probe line-start-mindist.ly score CG4). ⚠️ Keep this pinned when the taper goes: it must stay exact while the six-string half closes, or the fix moved the wrong thing.

line-start.clef-to-time.tab.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (+0.235 -> 0), paired with line-start.clef-to-time.treble as the CONTROL. Same quantity, same measurement, one difference: a TabStaff under the notation staff. LilyPond's TAB clef is an ordinary Clef grob (ly/engraver-init.ly TabStaff clefGlyph = "clefs.tab") and is WIDER than the G clef -- origin-to-ink-right 2.8 against 2.565 -- so it widens the shared Clef break-align group and pushes the meter column (Clef.space-alist time-signature extra-space 1.52) right with it. Rendered on 2.26.0: notation CLEF anchor 0.800 (ink 0.800..3.365), TABCLEF anchor 0.800 (ink 1.000..3.600), TIME anchor 5.120 => clef->time 4.320000, against the treble control's 4.085000. The 0.235000 between them IS the TAB clef's ink advantage; the pair's LilyPond side differs by exactly that, so a Lily# reading that made them EQUAL was the defect. OPENED at residual +0.235: SpacingRules.MaxClefWidth walked only NON-tab staves, so the tab staff contributed nothing to the group however wide its clef, and Lily# printed the control's 4.085 here too. THE FIX: the group extent (SpacingRules.ClefGroupExtent) folds every staff that engraves a clef INCLUDING tab, taking clefs.tab's LILC bbox (0.2 . 2.8) -- newly generated, since the tab clef had never been in the metrics table -- and the renderer draws clefs.tab UNSCALED at that same group anchor, so the width booked is the width drawn. Before the fix Lily# scaled the glyph to the staff height (tabHeight/5.78) and drew it at systemStartX with no LeftEdge->clef 0.8 at all, which is why it could not be booked. Verified against the tab staff LilyPond actually draws (probe line-start-mindist.ly, scores CGT and CG4: staff-space 1.5, clef 5.760000 tall unscaled and centred on the middle line, overhanging a 4-string staff). Impact: every tab score re-bases -- the TAB clef changes size and moves onto the clef column, and on notation+tab scores the meter and first note move 0.235 right.

line-start.clef-to-time.percussion.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (+0.565000 -> 0), the LAST remnant of defect-3 (the PERCUSSION clef). Unlike a pitched clef, whose ink starts at the grob origin (ext-left 0), the percussion glyph's ink begins 0.67 ss RIGHT of its origin. Rendered on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score DCP): CLEF anchor 0.13, ext (0.67 . 2.0) => ink-left 0.8 (the LeftEdge->clef offset every clef shares), ink-right 2.13; the meter binds 1.52 off that ink right edge => TIME at 3.65, so the clef-anchor -> time-anchor distance is 3.65 - 0.13 = 3.520000. OPENED at residual +0.565000 (predicted to the digit before measuring): Lily# reserved GClefWidth (2.565) for the percussion clef via LineStartClefWidth's fallback AND drew the glyph at its origin (x + ClefGlyphXOffset) without the 0.67 ink-left offset, so its clef anchor sat at 0.8 (not 0.13) and its time flowed to 0.8 + 2.565 + 1.52 = 4.885 => the twin read 4.085 (the treble value), residual 4.085 - 3.52 = +0.565 -- EQUAL to the treble twin, the cross-check that both the width AND the origin were the fixed-treble approximation. THE FIX (two threaded quantities): (1) GlyphMetricsGenerated now carries ClefPercussion (LILC bbox 0.67,-1.0,2.0,1.0, extracted from the font like every other clef) and GlyphMetrics.LineStartClefWidth returns its ink WIDTH ClefPercussion.Right - Left = 1.33 (not the 2.565 fallback), so the shared clef column and the meter it break-aligns reserve the real width; (2) GlyphMetrics.ClefInkLeft returns ClefPercussion.Left 0.67 and SharedRenderer.DrawClef draws the glyph at x + ClefGlyphXOffset - ClefInkLeft, shifting the percussion origin to 0.13 so its ink-left lands on the shared 0.8 column exactly as LilyPond places it. Both are no-ops for the pitched clefs (ink-left 0). MEASURED after: Lily# 3.520000000, residual -0.000000000 EXACT. Impact: the percussion line-start meter and metered first note move ~1.235 LEFT (the over-reserved 2.565 - 1.33) and the percussion clef GLYPH shifts 0.67 left onto its true ink column; snapshots with a percussion clef (drum-groove) re-base. This closes defect-3 for every clef family.

line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-al.why: CLOSED TO EXACT THIS SESSION (was ~3.05, now 0). Cross-staff meter alignment in a grand staff whose staves carry DIFFERENT keys (upper transposed to D major = 2 sharps, lower concert C major = none). LilyPond break-aligns the TimeSignature into ONE column spanning both staves -- the KeySignature break-align GROUP extent is the union across staves (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, g->extent(g,X_AXIS) over the group; :242 offsets the next column from extents[idx][RIGHT], the union RIGHT), so both meters print PAST the WIDEST key, at the same x. RENDERED on 2.26.0 (barline-spacing.ly score TSA): both TIME grobs at x=7.6534 (CLEF 0.8, the shared KEY column 4.3034 even for the empty lower key, HEAD 11.3534) -- spread 0. This is a METRIC-FREE probe: it compares two glyph anchors in the SAME render, depending on no ink width, so LP's 0 is exact by alignment, not a measured distance. BEFORE the fix Lily# spaced each staff's meter off its OWN key, so the concert staff's meter sat ~3.05 LEFT of the transposed staff's (its fixture transpose-multistaff read upper 8.05 vs lower 5.0) -- the fixture comment even claimed 'Verified against LilyPond', falsified by rendering LP. THE FIX: SharedRenderer draws every staff's meter at the system-wide MAX of the per-staff meter x (sharedTimeX = the widest key's column), so a same-key score is byte-identical and only differing-per-staff-key scores re-align. MEASURED after: Lily# spread 0.000000, EXACT. The absolute meter x also now matches LP (see line-start.clef-to-time.keyed): the KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 that DrawKeySignature once added to the drawn column, but the break-align reservation omitted, was removed so draw and reserve are one key-ink-measured model.

line-start.clef-to-time.keyed.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION (+0.4 -> 0). Clef -> time on a KEYED staff (D major, 2 sharps): the meter binds through the KEY, not the clef -- KeySignature.space-alist (time-signature . (extra-space . 1.15)) off the key's ink RIGHT edge, no pad. Rendered on 2.26.0: CLEF 0.8, KEY 4.185 (ext 2.2), TIME 7.535 => clef->time 6.735. The Lily# meter drew a KeySigTrailingGap 0.4 further right than the layout reserved -- a draw-vs-reserve split (SS 5.2.1(2)): DrawKeySignature returned key-ink + 0.4 for the meter to flow from, while BreakAlignSpacing reserved the note column off key-ink alone. THE FIX: the drawn time column (SharedRenderer.sharedTimeX) now uses KeySignatureInkWidth (the ink alone, = the reservation), and DrawKeySignature's now-dead +0.4 return was dropped. MEASURED after: Lily# 6.735000000, residual 0.000000000 EXACT -- confirming Lily#'s key ink width already matches LP's 2.2, so the 0.4 pad was the whole of the split. Impact: every keyed score's drawn line-start meter moves 0.4 LEFT onto the reserved column (first notes, layout-driven, do not move); snapshots with a key + time signature re-base.

line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-k.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-0.095264567 -> 0 exact). The CONTROL of the KCS/KCC custom-key pair was non-zero the moment it opened -- the keyed+metered line-start time->first-note regime had no point. LilyPond: head at the meter's ink RIGHT + 2.0 (TimeSignature.space-alist (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), natural length under ragged-right): TIME 7.535, ink 1.700000, HEAD 11.235 => 3.700000. The residual went through TWO wrong decompositions before the PNG showed the truth: (1) 'gap 1.9 vs 2.0' -- refuted by reading FirstNoteSpring, whose time arm is (2.0, 1.0) = LP exactly; (2) 'grob ext vs Pango advance of the digits' -- refuted by LOOKING at the render: Lily# (like LilyPond) draws the default 4/4 as the common-time C GLYPH, not digits. LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44 -- scm/time-signature-settings.scm:954-964,981-982 make-c-time-signature-markup) and every other fraction as \number markup; the C44 LILC ink is 1.700000 (extracted from the font, = the measured grob ext to the digit). Lily# drew the C glyph but reserved the DIGIT path's Pango width 1.604735433. THE FIX: GetTimeSigWidth mirrors LP's style branch -- (4,4)->TimeSigCommon.Width, (2,2)->TimeSigCutCommon.Width (both LILC 1.7, newly extracted), else the Pango digit path unchanged (barline.next.time-change-to-notehead stays exact on it); DrawTimeSignature's invented flat 2.0 return replaced by the same widths. Every 4/4 first system's notes move +0.095264567 right (snapshot re-base, justified by this key and cut-common going exact).

system.knee-beam-notes.why: EXACT, and what it settles is that a KNEE is a structural divergence that does not reach the page. LilyPond leaves only CROSS-staff grobs out of the vertical skylines (lily/axis-group-interface.cc:850-858, its own comment), so a same-staff kneed Beam and its Stems ARE in them; Lily# seeds NEITHER — SkylineBuilder.AddBeamsToSkyline skips IsKnee and BeamedItemsToSuppress skips it too, so each member keeps the per-note FIXED 3.5 stem, in the member's OWN direction (AddNoteBoxToSkylines takes note.StemUp). WHY THAT SUBSTITUTE IS ENOUGH HERE: a knee's stems point INWARD — the low note stems up to the beam, the high note down to it — so the band and both stems live BETWEEN the two heads, and the heads are the envelope either way. LilyPond's own numbers say the same: its kneed ink TOP is 8.545000 above the refpoint, exactly d''''`s head (8.0 + 0.545), with no beam above it. THE POINT IS NOT SITTING ON A FLOOR, which is what makes it worth keeping: 18.090000 is neither the 12.000000 system-system basic-distance nor the 20.285000 the SAME music gives with the knee forbidden (\override Beam.auto-knee-gap = #100, probe book KNEC) — so the knee is worth 2.195000 of vertical room and this entry is measuring the kneed envelope itself. A future port that seeds the knee's band with the wrong geometry moves this number. PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN and held: exact. ⚠️ TWO FIXTURE ERRORS ARE RECORDED IN THE PROBE HEADER, both the same trap: the first control was the same shape WITHOUT the leap (so its 6.090000 was almost all d''''`s own ink, not the knee), and the first pair had 4 bars with an explicit break where Lily# fitted all four on ONE system and the gap could not be read at all.

line-start.clef-to-time.mixed-key-grand-.why: EXACT, and it is a CONTROL for a defect that lives one layer away — raised so the fix for that defect cannot be applied in the wrong direction. WHAT IS MEASURED: clef to meter on a grand staff where only the UPPER staff engraves a signature (its part is transposed, so it prints D major = 2 sharps, beside a concert-pitch C-major lower staff). The distance therefore SPANS a key column that the score-level key knows nothing about — the score key here is C major, which books nothing at all. LilyPond dumps CLEF 0.800000, KEY 4.303400 (ext 2.200000), TIME 7.653400, first HEAD 11.353400; Lily# reproduces 6.853400 to 9 digits, because its line-start reservation unions the staves' OWN signatures (SpacingRules.WidestActiveKeyInk / ActiveKeyInkForStaff, the model built for line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-keyed). ⚠️ THE SIBLING POINT CANNOT SEE THIS: line-start.time-signature-cross-staff-alignment is an identity (both meters at one x) and holds however wide the shared key column is, INCLUDING not at all. THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS AGAINST: the BREAK GATE prices the same line start from score.LeadingKey instead (SystemBreaker.cs:66-69, IncrementalCompiler.cs:170-174), which on this score books 6.703400 against the layout's 9.353400 — 2.650000 short, being the key's 2.200000 plus the Clef->Key and Key->Time gaps that only open when a signature is engraved. That is a Lily#-internal disagreement with no LilyPond number of its own (LilyPond's breaker uses the real spacing — constrained-breaking.cc — so it HAS no second model), and it is held by SpacingInvariantTests.BreakGateAndLayout_PriceTheSameLineStart rather than by a corpus point: its only visible consequence is a line break, and a break flips inside a 2.650000 window, which would make a knife-edge ledger entry. When that gate is fixed, the fix must move the GATE up to this number and not this number down to the gate — which is what this point exists to say.

line-start.time-to-first-note.custom-key.why: CLOSED IN TWO STEPS THE SAME SESSION (-2.745264567 -> -0.095264567 -> 0 exact; the second step is the shared C-glyph meter width, see line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key).The defect: the same two sharps declared as a CUSTOM signature reserved NO key column, because the reservation read KeySignature.Sharps only (WidestActiveKeySharps and the KeySignatureChangeItem scan dropped Custom; a custom key is KeySignature(0, custom), MeasureCollector.Form.cs:385) while the draw walk drew the signature -- the drawn meter overlapped the first note. THE FIX: one key-width model. SpacingRules.KeySignatureInkWidth(KeySignature) is now the single source (custom = per-glyph advance sum, standard = count x advance); SolvePrefixColumns/CalculatePrefixWidth/FirstNoteSpring take the key INK width instead of a sharps count; WidestActiveKey returns the full KeySignature record, widest by ink (the break-align group extent is an ink union, break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142), and preserves Custom through mid-piece key changes; MultiStaffScore.LeadingKey replaces LeadingKeySharps. LilyPond's KCC dump is byte-identical to KCS (one key model, keyAlterations) and Lily# now mirrors that structure. The whole existing corpus is byte-invariant (standard keys compute the identical width; zero snapshots moved).

line-start.time-to-first-note.cut-common.why: OPENED EXACT as the cut-common half of the C-glyph width pair (with line-start.time-to-first-note.standard-key). LilyPond's default style prints ONLY 2/2 and 4/4 as glyphs (timesig.C22/C44, make-c-time-signature-markup); C22's LILC ink is 1.700000 like C44's, so time -> first note is 3.700000 for BOTH -- the pair's equality is the cross-check that the two C widths ride one (glyph) path while every other fraction stays on the Pango digit path. Lily# reserved 2/2 from the digit table too (GetTimeSigWidth max digit '2' = 1.4657 Pango) under a drawn cut-C glyph; the same fix (GetTimeSigWidth's LP-style branch) closes both.

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.sharps.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). The ossia (no clef on its first appearance) above a keyed main staff: its key signature must sit in the ONE KeySignature break-align column spanning the system, exactly like the grand-staff clef/time columns (break-alignment-interface.cc:141-142, group extent = union across staves). METRIC-FREE: ossia key X minus main key X in the same render; LilyPond prints 0 (OKEY anchor == KEY anchor == 4.185, for the NR fontSize+staff-space recipe AND under \magnifyStaff -- probe scores OKN/OKM). The PREDICTION written before the LP dump said 'LeftEdge -> key-signature extra-space 0.8 (define-grobs.scm:2097)' -- the dump REFUTED it: column sharing wins; the 0.8 alist entry never binds because the system-wide Clef column exists (the main staff has a clef). Lily# drew the ossia key at systemStartX + Clef->Key 0.82 off a clef that was not there. THE FIX: the drawn walk places every staff's key at the SHARED key column (sharedKeyX = widest-clef right + Clef->Key), the same expression the reservation's SolvePrefixColumns KeyX carries -- for a staff with a clef this is byte-identical to the former per-staff walk, so only the ossia moved. ALSO fixed with it, per the coordinate-frame rule: the ossia signature's INTERNAL glyph advances were unscaled (1.1 real ss inside a magstep(-3) staff -- mixed frames); DrawKeySignature now scales its advances by the staff's notation scale, matching LP's scaled stencil (OKN dump: OKEY ink 1.5558 ~ 2.2 x magstep(-3); the sub-0.1% remainder is LP's design-size font metrics, the clef-sliver family, not opened here).

line-start.ossia-key-alignment.flats.why: OPENED AND CLOSED THE SAME SESSION (-3.365 -> 0 exact). Flats half of the ossia key-alignment pair (B-flat major; see the sharps entry for the mechanism and the fix). LilyPond: OKEY == KEY == 4.185, offset 0 -- the same 0 as sharps, the pair's content-independence cross-check. Lily# now prints 0 on both halves: the shared key column is one expression, so it cannot depend on the key's content.

line-start.time-to-first-note.tab-concer.why: CLOSED TO EXACT (+0.400000 -> 0) by porting merge_springs. CONTROL of the tab-key pair (a tab staff beside a concert notation staff, both in C major). It opened NON-ZERO and its residual was NOT the defect the pair was cut for: the LilyPond value is 3.300000, not the single-staff 3.700000 of KCS/KC2, because the line-start spring is merge_springs (spring.cc:104) AVERAGING one wish per staff and the two staves wish for different things -- their last prefatory grob differs. Notation staff: last grob TimeSignature, (first-note . (semi-shrink-space . 2.0)), staff-spacing.cc:193-198 -> fixed 6.82+1.0, ideal 8.82. Tab staff: last grob Clef, (first-note . (minimum-fixed-space . 5.0)), :183-187 -> ink-left 1.0 + max(2.6, 5.0) = 6.0, then the SHARED min_dist floor (:212-215, 0.3 + min_dist) lifts it to 8.02. Average (8.82+8.02)/2 = 8.42 = TIME ink right 6.82 + 1.6. Two ORDINARY staves keep 3.700000 exactly (measured on a treble+bass twin: TIME 5.0034 -> HEAD 8.7034) because equal wishes average to themselves -- which is why no earlier multi-staff point could see this. THE FIX, ported literally: spacing-spanner.cc:492-517 breakable_column_spacing collects one Staff_spacing wish per staff from the left column's spacing-wishes and ends in merge_springs, so LineStartColumn.LineStartSpring now builds one wish per staff (LineStartColumn.PrefatoryGrobs -> Spacing_interface::extremal_break_aligned_grob, spacing-interface.cc:190-230, which SKIPS empty extents -- that is why a tab staff's stencil-less TimeSignature drops out and its TAB clef becomes the extremal grob) and Spring.MergeSprings averages them (spring.cc:101-129, N at once). The prediction written before the measurement -- both halves exact, no other ledger point moving -- held for this half to 15 digits and for every other point; the keyed half kept a small residual from a SECOND defect, recorded there.
